title: Describing and comparing
goal: Settle the 好 we parked back in Unit 1: Cantonese adjectives are verbs, take no 係, and need a prop. Then compare things with 過, 最 and 啲.
bekal: use adjectives without 係, propped up with 好
compare two things with A + adjective + 過 + B

dialogs.title: 對話 1 — Hong Kong and Jakarta
dialogs.intro: Wong Lai asks about Jakarta. The whole conversation is a comparison — notice that there isn't a single 係 in front of an adjective.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [雅加達|Ngaa5 gaa1 daat6][熱唔熱㗎|jit6 m4 jit6 gaa3]？
lines.id: Is Jakarta hot?
lines.literal: Jakarta — hot — not — hot — emphasis.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [好熱|Hou2 jit6]。[但係|Daan6 hai6][香港夏天|Hoeng1 gong2 haa6 tin1][熱過雅加達|jit6 gwo3 Ngaa5 gaa1 daat6]。
lines.id: It is. But Hong Kong summers are hotter than Jakarta.
lines.literal: filler — hot. but — Hong-Kong — summer — hot — past — Jakarta.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [真係咩|Zan1 hai6 me1]？[點解呀|Dim2 gaai2 aa3]？
lines.id: Really? How come?
lines.literal: real — is — really. how — explain — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [因為好潮濕|Jan1 wai6 hou2 ciu4 sap1]。[雅加達熱|Ngaa5 gaa1 daat6 jit6]，[但係冇咁焗|daan6 hai6 mou5 gam3 guk6]。

lines.literal: because — filler — humid. Jakarta — hot, but — not-have — so — muggy.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [咁|Gam2][邊度嘅嘢好食啲呀|bin1 dou6 ge3 je5 hou2 sik6 di1 aa3]？

lines.literal: then — which — place — possessive — stuff — good — eat — a-bit — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [好難講|Hou2 naan4 gong2]。[香港嘢貴好多|Hoeng1 gong2 je5 gwai3 hou2 do1]，[但係好方便|daan6 hai6 hou2 fong1 bin6]。
lines.id: Hard to say. Things in Hong Kong are much more expensive, but really convenient.
lines.literal: filler — hard — say. Hong-Kong — stuff — expensive — filler — much, but — filler — handy.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [你最鍾意|Nei5 zeoi3 zung1 ji3][香港邊樣嘢呀|Hoeng1 gong2 bin1 joeng6 je5 aa3]？

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [地鐵|Dei6 tit3]！[快過雅加達好多|Faai3 gwo3 Ngaa5 gaa1 daat6 hou2 do1]，[又唔使塞車|jau6 m4 sai2 sak1 ce1]。
lines.id: The MTR! Much faster than Jakarta, and no traffic jams.
lines.literal: MTR. fast — past — Jakarta — filler — much, also — not — need — jam — vehicle.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [咁最唔鍾意呢|Gam2 zeoi3 m4 zung1 ji3 ne1]？
lines.id: And what do you like least?
lines.literal: then — most — not — like — what.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [間屋太細喇|Gaan1 uk1 taai3 sai3 laa3]。[我間房細過我以前個廁所|Ngo5 gaan1 fong2 sai3 gwo3 ngo5 ji5 cin4 go3 ci3 so2]！
lines.id: The flats are too small. My room is smaller than my old toilet!
lines.literal: classifier — house — too — small — already. I — classifier — room — small — past — I — before — classifier — toilet.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [哈哈|Haa1 haa1]！[歡迎嚟到香港|Fun1 jing4 lei4 dou3 Hoeng1 gong2]！
lines.id: Haha! Welcome to Hong Kong!
lines.literal: happy — welcome — come — arrive — Hong-Kong.

notes: **⚠️ Cantonese adjectives are verbs. Never put 係 in front of them.** [我好攰|Ngo5 hou2 gui6] = I'm tired. 我係攰 is wrong and sounds like a word-for-word translation of “I am tired”. This is the number-one mistake English speakers make in this whole module.

**[好|hou2] before an adjective often isn't “very” but a required prop.** [我好攰|Ngo5 hou2 gui6] just means “I'm tired”, not “I'm very tired”. A bare adjective — [我攰|Ngo5 gui6] — sounds unfinished, like a sentence cut off halfway.

**If you really mean “very”, use something else.** [好好攰|hou2 hou2 gui6] (really tired), [非常攰|fei1 soeng4 gui6] (extremely tired, a bit formal), [攰死喇|gui6 sei2 laa3] (dead tired), or stretch out the 好: *hoooou2 gui6*.
**[真係咩|Zan1 hai6 me1]？ = “really?”** Remember 咩 from Unit 1: the surprise particle. [真係|zan1 hai6] = truly, really. [真係好靚|Zan1 hai6 hou2 leng3] = really lovely.

**[冇咁|mou5 gam3] + adjective = “not as …”.** [佢冇我咁高|Keoi5 mou5 ngo5 gam3 gou1] = he isn't as tall as me. This is how Cantonese makes negative comparisons, and it looks nothing like the positive comparison with 過.
**[好難講|hou2 naan4 gong2] = “hard to say”.** Adjective + verb pattern: [好難學|hou2 naan4 hok6] (hard to learn), [好易做|hou2 ji6 zou6] (easy to do), [好好食|hou2 hou2 sik6] (tasty, good to eat).
**[又|jau6] = “and also, on top of that”.** [又平又好食|jau6 peng4 jau6 hou2 sik6] = cheap and tasty. The paired 又…又… is the most natural way to string two adjectives together.

grammars.title: Adjectives: no 係, with a prop
body: In Cantonese, adjectives behave like verbs: they can stand alone as the core of a sentence, are negated with 唔, and are asked about with A-唔-A.

head: Form
Example
Meaning
rows: [佢高唔高呀|Keoi5 gou1 m4 gou1 aa3]？

after: ⚠️ **Notice that negatives and questions DROP the 好.** [佢好高|Keoi5 hou2 gou1] but [佢唔高|Keoi5 m4 gou1] — not 佢唔好高. The prop only appears in positive statements.

**[幾|gei2] before an adjective means “quite”** — not “how many”. [幾好|gei2 hou2] = quite good; [幾靚|gei2 leng3] = quite pretty. What tells it apart from 幾 “how many” is what follows: an adjective, not a classifier.

grammars.title: Comparing: 過, 冇咁, 一樣, 最
body: 🇭🇰 Spoken Cantonese compares with [過|gwo3], placed **after** the adjective. The Mandarin-style 比 is understood in Hong Kong too, but it sounds like written language.

head: Relation
Structure
Example
rows: [我高過佢|Ngo5 gou1 gwo3 keoi5]。 I'm taller than him.
A is much more … than B
A + adj. + 過 + B + 好多
[香港貴過印尼好多|Hoeng1 gong2 gwai3 gwo3 Jan3 nei4 hou2 do1]。
A is a little more … than B
A + adj. + 過 + B + 少少
[佢快過我少少|Keoi5 faai3 gwo3 ngo5 siu2 siu2]。
A is not as … as B
A + 冇 + B + 咁 + adj.
[佢冇我咁高|Keoi5 mou5 ngo5 gam3 gou1]。
A + 同 + B + 一樣 + adj.
[呢個同嗰個一樣貴|Ni1 go3 tung4 go2 go3 jat1 joeng6 gwai3]。
[平啲|peng4 di1] cheaper · [快啲|faai3 di1] faster

after: **[啲|di1] says “more” without naming what you're comparing with.** [平啲|peng4 di1] = cheaper (than the last one); [行快啲|haang4 faai3 di1] = walk faster. You used this when haggling in Unit 3 and asking people to speak slowly in Unit 2.
⚠️ **Don't combine 過 with 好.** [我高過佢|Ngo5 gou1 gwo3 keoi5] is right; 我好高過佢 is wrong. The 好 prop disappears as soon as there's a comparison.
**Asking for a comparison: [邊個…啲呀|bin1 go3 … di1 aa3]？** [邊個平啲呀|Bin1 go3 peng4 di1 aa3]？ = which one is cheaper? [邊個最好呀|Bin1 go3 zeoi3 hou2 aa3]？ = which one is best?

dialogs.title: 對話 2 — Choosing a phone
dialogs.intro: Andi buys a new phone in Sham Shui Po. Comparison practice disguised as shopping — every line uses a different comparison pattern.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [唔該|M4 goi1]，[呢兩部電話|ni1 loeng5 bou6 din6 waa2][邊部好啲呀|bin1 bou6 hou2 di1 aa3]？
lines.id: Excuse me, which of these two phones is better?
lines.literal: excuse-me, this — two — classifier — phone — which — classifier — good — a-bit — huh.

lines.speaker: 店員:
lines.text: [呢部新啲|Ni1 bou6 san1 di1]，[但係貴成千蚊|daan6 hai6 gwai3 seng4 cin1 man1]。
lines.id: This one is newer, but it's a full thousand dollars more.
lines.literal: this — classifier — new — a-bit, but — expensive — whole — thousand — dollar.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [嗰部呢|Go2 bou6 ne1]？[平幾多呀|Peng4 gei2 do1 aa3]？
lines.id: And that one? How much cheaper?
lines.literal: that — classifier — how. cheap — how — much — huh.

lines.speaker: 店員:
lines.text: [平一千二|Peng4 jat1 cin1 ji6]，[但係個電池冇咁耐用|daan6 hai6 go3 din6 ci4 mou5 gam3 noi6 jung6]。
lines.id: 1,200 cheaper, but the battery doesn't last as long.
lines.literal: cheap — one — thousand — two, but — classifier — electric — pool — not-have — so — long — use.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [個相機呢|Go3 soeng2 gei1 ne1]？[邊部影相靚啲呀|Bin1 bou6 jing2 soeng2 leng3 di1 aa3]？
lines.id: What about the camera? Which one takes better photos?
lines.literal: classifier — photo — machine — how. which — classifier — shoot — photo — good — a-bit — huh.

lines.speaker: 店員:
lines.text: [兩部差唔多|Loeng5 bou6 caa1 m4 do1]。[其實|Kei4 sat6][舊嗰部|gau6 go2 bou6][抵好多|dai2 hou2 do1]。
lines.id: They're about the same. Honestly, the older one is much better value.
lines.literal: two — classifier — differ — not — much. actually — old — that — classifier — worth — filler — much.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [你好老實喎|Nei5 hou2 lou5 sat6 wo3]！[咁我要嗰部啦|Gam2 ngo5 jiu3 go2 bou6 laa1]。
lines.id: You're honest! Then I'll take that one.
lines.literal: you — filler — old — real — you-know. then — I — want — that — classifier — go-on.

lines.speaker: 店員:
lines.text: [好眼光|Hou2 ngaan5 gwong1]。[要唔要保護貼呀|Jiu3 m4 jiu3 bou2 wu6 tip3 aa3]？
lines.id: Good choice. Want a screen protector?
lines.literal: good — eye — light. want — not — want — protect — guard — stick — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [幾多錢呀|Gei2 do1 cin2 aa3]？[平啲得唔得|Peng4 di1 dak1 m4 dak1]？
lines.id: How much? Can you go a bit lower?
lines.literal: how — much — money — huh. cheap — a-bit — can — not — can.

lines.speaker: 店員:
lines.text: [買電話送埋|Maai5 din6 waa2 sung3 maai4]，[唔使錢|m4 sai2 cin2]！
lines.id: It comes free with the phone — no charge!
lines.literal: buy — phone — give — along, not — need — money.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [多謝晒|Do1 ze6 saai3]！[你間舖頭|Nei5 gaan1 pou3 tau2][係我見過最好嘅|hai6 ngo5 gin3 gwo3 zeoi3 hou2 ge3]。
lines.id: Thanks so much! Your shop is the best I've ever seen.
lines.literal: thank — completely. you — classifier — shop — is — I — see — ever — most — good — possessive.

notes: **[成|seng4] before a number means “a whole …, as much as”.** [成千蚊|seng4 cin1 man1] = a whole thousand dollars; [成日|seng4 jat6] = all day long (you know it from Unit 2). It stresses that the amount is big.
**[平一千二|peng4 jat1 cin1 ji6] = “1,200 cheaper”.** The difference goes right after the adjective, with no linking word at all. [高兩吋|gou1 loeng5 cyun3] = two inches taller.
**[差唔多|caa1 m4 do1] = “about the same, almost”.** One of the words you'll hear most. [差唔多啦|Caa1 m4 do1 laa1] = yeah, more or less; [差唔多三點|caa1 m4 do1 saam1 dim2] = almost three o'clock.

**[抵|dai2] = worth it, good value.** 🇭🇰 A very Hong Kong word with no single-word equivalent in English. [好抵|hou2 dai2] = a bargain for the quality; [唔抵|m4 dai2] = not worth it. Its opposite isn't “expensive” but “a rip-off”.
**[其實|kei4 sat6] = actually.** It stands at the start of the sentence and signals that what follows isn't what you'd expect.
**[好眼光|hou2 ngaan5 gwong1] = “good choice”, literally “good eye”.** The standard compliment from seller to buyer. A smile or [多謝|do1 ze6] is enough as a reply.

**[送|sung3] = to give free as a bonus.** [買一送一|maai5 jat1 sung3 jat1] = buy one get one free. [埋|maai4] after it means “along with it”. ⚠️ 送 also means “to see someone off, take someone”: [我送你返屋企|Ngo5 sung3 nei5 faan1 uk1 kei2] = I'll take you home.

grammars.title: Adjective pairs you need
body: Cantonese builds many abstract nouns from a pair of opposite adjectives — [大細|daai6 sai3] = size, [長短|coeng4 dyun2] = length. Learning them in pairs is faster than one by one.
after: 🇭🇰 **[靚|leng3] works for anything nice to look at** — people, clothes, photos, views, even handwriting. It's much broader than “pretty” in English.
**[矮|ai2] for short people, [短|dyun2] for short things.** Swapping them sounds funny: 佢好短 sounds as if the person has been chopped down.

blocks.text: Weather is the number-one small-talk topic in Hong Kong, and for good reason: the city has a brutal summer, a typhoon season that rewrites everyone's plans, and a short winter that suddenly feels biting.

head: Weather sentence
Meaning
rows: [今日天氣點呀|Gam1 jat6 tin1 hei3 dim2 aa3]？
[聽日會唔會落雨呀|Ting1 jat6 wui5 m4 wui5 lok6 jyu5 aa3]？
[今日凍過琴日|Gam1 jat6 dung3 gwo3 kam4 jat6]。

blocks.title: Typhoons: the words people actually use
items: 🇭🇰 **[八號風球|baat3 hou6 fung1 kau4] — typhoon signal no. 8.** Once it's raised, offices close, schools shut, and public transport stops. The sentence you'll hear all day: [今晚掛八號|Gam1 maan5 gwaa3 baat3 hou6] = signal 8 goes up tonight.
[三號風球|saam1 hou6 fung1 kau4] — signal 3, everything still runs as normal.
[黑色暴雨|hak1 sik1 bou6 jyu5] — black rainstorm warning, with an impact similar to signal 8.
[今日返唔返工呀|Gam1 jat6 faan1 m4 faan1 gung1 aa3]？ — “Are we going to work today?” The most common question in office WhatsApp groups on a windy morning.

blocks.text: Comparisons come alive when you use them on people and things you know. You can fill the patterns below with the people around you right away.

head: Pattern
Example
rows: [我大佬高過我|Ngo5 daai6 lou2 gou1 gwo3 ngo5]。 My older brother is taller than me.
A + 冇 + B + 咁 + adj.
[我冇佢咁叻|Ngo5 mou5 keoi5 gam3 lek1]。 I'm not as smart as her.
[我同佢一樣高|Ngo5 tung4 keoi5 jat1 joeng6 gou1]。 I'm as tall as him.
[佢係我哋入面最叻嗰個|Keoi5 hai6 ngo5 dei6 jap6 min6 zeoi3 lek1 go2 go3]。
[佢又叻又勤力|Keoi5 jau6 lek1 jau6 kan4 lik6]。 She's smart and hardworking.
[佢係好好嘅人|Keoi5 hai6 hou2 hou2 ge3 jan4]。 He's a really nice person.

items: [叻|lek1] smart, skilled · [勤力|kan4 lik6] hardworking · [懶|laan5] lazy
[好人|hou2 jan4] kind · [惡|ok3] fierce · [細心|sai3 sam1] careful
[開心|hoi1 sam1] happy · [唔開心|m4 hoi1 sam1] sad · [嬲|nau1] angry
[攰|gui6] tired · [悶|mun6] bored · [緊張|gan2 zoeng1] nervous
🇭🇰 [叻|lek1] is the praise most often given to children and to anyone who's just finished something. [好叻呀|Hou2 lek1 aa3]！ = well done!

wave: Five minutes before Unit 9: compare five pairs of things in front of you right now — two glasses, two books, two people in a photo — each with a different pattern: 過, 冇…咁, 一樣, 最 and …啲. Then say five sentences about yourself today using adjectives without 係: 我好攰、我好肚餓、我唔開心. If your hand is itching to write 係 in there, that's the sign you need this drill.
